summary: Nelson County fire tower on Sugar Loaf Mountain, used for about half a century and since removed, according to a News & Advance report.

facts.status_note: The News & Advance reports the tower was removed; no source I read describes what, if anything, remains at the site.

evidence.supports: listed as Tower Gone, Sugar Loaf Mountain (Nelson), Nelson County
evidence.quote: Sugar Loaf Mountain (Nelson) Nelson 37.78261 -78.82072 Tower Gone

evidence.supports: tower removed; used for about half a century
evidence.quote: After being used to keep residents of Nelson County safe for about half a century, the old fire tower located atop Sugar Loaf Mountain has been removed.

evidence.supports: HighRock's page is titled for a Nelson County fire tower
the tower had sat abandoned for years; HighRock restored it
evidence.quote: A historic fire tower in the heart of Virginia's Blue Ridge Mountains has sat abandoned for years.

evidence.supports: HighRock turned it into a rustic mountain retreat
evidence.quote: into a rustic mountain retreat for those looking to unplug

evidence.supports: HighRock compares the retreat to a bed and breakfast
evidence.quote: a unique experience unlike that of any other bed & breakfast

sources.title: Old fire tower removed from Sugar Loaf Mountain

notes_for_editor: The removal is reported in the News & Advance summary line only. The article body is encoded on the page and was not decoded, so the removal date and the tower's build date are unknown and no events are recorded. The Sugar Loaf Mountain entry on the eastern lookout site covers Fayette County, Pennsylvania, a different tower. The HighRock tower names no mountain and is not linked to Sugar Loaf. A Facebook post in search results describes a Sugarloaf fire tower in the Shipman-Lovingston area; it was not read.
